Package dev.gmitch215.bytebox.locks

Class CompletableFuture<T>

java.lang.Object
dev.gmitch215.bytebox.locks.CompletableFuture<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the value type
All Implemented Interfaces:
CompletionStage<T>, Future<T>
public class CompletableFuture<T> extends Object implements Future<T>, CompletionStage<T>
java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture, which the class library does not carry.

Failures follow the JDK's wrapping: a stage that fails because of another is completed with a CompletionException around the cause, join() throws that, and get() unwraps it into an ExecutionException. supplyAsync(Supplier) runs the task on a new fiber, since there is no pool, and callbacks run on the fiber that completes the stage.

get(), get(long, TimeUnit) and join() suspend the caller, so they trap when no fiber is running, even on a future that is already done. The generated entry point builds the handler, a Durable Object and a Workflow on a fiber, so their constructors and the static initializers they trigger may call them.

When a whenComplete action throws on a stage that had already failed, the original failure stands and the action's is dropped; the JDK adds it as a suppressed exception, and Throwable.addSuppressed throws a NullPointerException on this runtime.

Left out: the *Async forms of the then methods, the *Either and *Both forms, orTimeout, completeAsync, the obtrude methods and the Java 19 additions. Calling one fails to link when the program is built.

Since:
1.0.3
